text:
Linus Ullmark gave Ottawa the win, and the numbers say New Jersey played the better game. NJD out-attempted OTT 80 to 41 and carried the stronger even-strength chances, 2.18 expected goals to 1.54. The shot-quality simulation had the Devils winning 66 percent of the time. Ullmark stopped 29 of 30 shots against 2.89 expected goals against, a gap of 1.89 goals in his favor, and Nico Daws allowed three on 2.01.

Ottawa's goals came early and late in the game's shape. Shane Pinto scored nine seconds into the second period, a 12 percent chance, and Stephen Halliday made it 2-0 on the power play at 8:40, a 16 percent look. OTT led in expected goals in that period, 1.34 to 0.78, which kept the Devils chasing. The Senators also blocked 30 shots to NJD's 10, and New Jersey took 13 penalty minutes to Ottawa's 4.

The third period went to New Jersey, 1.46 to 0.21 in expected goals, but Tim Stützle's tip-in at 11:10 made it 3-0 on a 9 percent chance. Arseny Gritsyuk answered at 14:59 for 3-1, and Tyler Kleven sealed it at 17:53 with a 44 percent chance, the best look of any goal in the game. Jesper Boqvist's 23 percent chance in the first period, stopped by Ullmark, was New Jersey's best miss.
